title: Crust-and-cushion-flora foundational survival strategy
scope: Foundational survival strategy of the K5 crust-and-cushion kingdom at qualitative grain; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Crust-and-cushion flora are low, slow, surface-hugging pioneers of bare and hostile surfaces: rock, stone, dead casings, walls, and scoured or disturbed ground.
Their two broad growth habits are thin surface crusts and dense dome cushions.

The kingdom's signature is metabolic shutdown and rapid revival: members tolerate near-total desiccation and deep freezing in a dormant state that can look entirely dead, then revive quickly on wetting or thaw.
Growth is extremely slow and confined to active windows; established cover is old cover.
Undisturbed crust and cushion cover is a qualitative mark of elapsed undisturbed time.
Their growth and decay initiate soil formation, opening succession for the other kingdoms.
boundaries: Crust, cushion, shutdown, and revival are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The strategy establishes no Earth lichen, moss, algae, or cushion-plant homology.
Species, forms, colours, dimensions, chemistry, energy capture, and reproduction remain open.

Shutdown limits, tolerance thresholds, revival speed, repeated-cycle costs, and failure modes remain open; shutdown is not invulnerability, and heat, scouring, burial, grazing, pollution, or repeated cycling can still kill.
Growth, colonisation, and soil-formation rates remain open; no cover is guaranteed to establish on any surface.

Cover as a mark of elapsed time is qualitative only; no calibrated dating method, rate constant, age reading, or in-world dating knowledge or practice is established, and disturbance, microclimate, and surface differences can confound apparent age.
Colonisation of dead tower casings, walls, and ruins is possible in principle; no particular structure, ruin, or site is established as colonised.
Cushion microclimate buffering and mineral binding remain possible branch details, not kingdom-wide properties.
No crust-and-cushion member is established as present, dominant, or absent at any particular location.
Grazing, pests, diseases, symbioses including any K6 partnership, and human uses remain open.
Earth and mythological inspiration remains author-facing; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Water, energy, nutrients, surface, time, disturbance, and competition remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Scenes can show grey apparently dead crusts reviving after rain and cushioned upland stone.
Long-undisturbed surfaces, including ruins, can carry heavy cover that reads qualitatively as age.
Soil initiation links the kingdom to later succession, recovery, and land-use development.
Every species, site, apparent age, and inference requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The strategy describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, dating method, spawn source, refill node, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What chemistry and structures implement shutdown and revival, and at what cost?
What growth, colonisation, and soil-formation rates apply across surfaces and climates?
Which surfaces do crusts versus cushions prefer, and how do they colonise dead casings and ruins?
Do cushion microclimate buffering or mineral binding occur in particular branches?
Does anyone in-world read cover as elapsed time, and how reliably?
Which grazers, pests, and symbioses shape pioneer cover?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C strategy cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Revival flora' on 2026-08-17.
